jobDescription: A developer-tools company with around 140 repositories is consolidating its CI and build tooling. The platform engineer maintains the CI runners and caches, manages the infrastructure in Terraform, supports product engineers through runbooks and a help channel, and will be the accountable technical lead for the next stage of the build migration. The team also runs an internal course for engineers adopting the new tooling and wants the platform engineer to design and teach it. The platform team has four engineers and reports to the director of engineering; product teams raise requests through the help channel and a fortnightly intake meeting.
requirements: Maintains CI runners and build caches for a multi-repository codebase.
Has been the accountable technical lead for a build-system or CI migration.
Writes runbooks and supports product engineers using the build tooling.
Manages CI infrastructure as code in Terraform through reviewed changes.
Has designed and run a formal training course for engineers.

evidence.text: Platform engineer at Quillstack from September 2020 to June 2024, maintaining the CI runners and the remote build cache for about 140 repositories, including the Linux and macOS runner pools.

Wrote the design document for moving the repositories from hand-written build scripts to Bazel; the architecture review board approved it in May 2022 with the candidate recorded as author and decision owner.
Scheduled and ran the repository-by-repository cutover over eleven weeks, holding a weekly go/no-go call with the affected team leads and pausing two cutovers that failed the cache-hit checks.
Managed the CI fleet through Terraform modules; every change went through a pull request reviewed by a second platform engineer.
Wrote the onboarding runbook for the new build setup and covered the platform help channel on a weekly rota, answering build questions from product engineers.

Work sample: a redacted copy of the Bazel migration design document, including its decision table (eight decisions, each initialled by the candidate as decider) and the per-repository cutover checklist.
HR verification note: employment dates at Quillstack were checked against the payroll record supplied by the former employer.

Reference check summary: the former director of engineering confirmed in writing that the candidate was the designated technical lead for the build-system migration from April 2022 to January 2023 and that the cutover schedule was the candidate's responsibility.

propositions.text: The candidate was the designated technical lead for the build-system migration and wrote its design document, which the architecture review board approved with the candidate as decision owner.
propositions.rationale: The written reference confirms the lead designation, and the resume and design-document extract record the approval and the decisions.

propositions.text: The candidate scheduled and ran the repository-by-repository cutover over eleven weeks, with a weekly go/no-go call with the affected team leads.
propositions.rationale: The resume describes the cutover and the reference confirms the schedule was the candidate's responsibility.

propositions.text: The candidate managed the CI fleet through Terraform modules, with every change reviewed by a second platform engineer.
propositions.rationale: The resume states the tooling and the review control.

gold.expectedGap: The candidate wrote an onboarding runbook and covered the help channel; designing and running a formal training course is not documented.
gold.expectedBoundaryNote: Keep the documented technical-lead designation, the approved design and the cutover responsibility; describe the support work as a runbook and help-channel rota rather than a training course.
followUpTargets: Ask whether the candidate has designed or delivered structured training for engineers, and what it covered.
